# Deferred-Anchor Registry

> The canonical source of truth for every `D-*` anchor cited in `src/` but
> deferred to a future cycle. The leading underscore sorts this file before
> the numbered plans in directory listings — call this out as the registry,
> not a plan. Per-plan §3.1 rows are still the preferred home for anchors
> whose feature area maps cleanly onto a plan; this file catches the orphans
> + cross-cutting anchors that don't belong to any single plan.
>
> **CI/pre-commit guard** (`tools/check-anchor-registry.{sh,ps1}`): every
> `D-*` identifier appearing in `src/` MUST resolve to a row in this file
> OR a citation in any `.plans/*.md`. Pre-fix this recurred TWICE
> (memory: "the same gap silent-failure caught for MULTI-PAGE-GOT").
> The guard makes the system enforce the discipline — same shape as the
> agnosticism veto + the `CallConv` static_assert.
>
> **★ ANCHOR-NAME RULE — READ BEFORE INVENTING A `D-*` NAME (documented 2026-07-28, TF-C81; it was
> load-bearing and unwritten until it bit).** The guard's regex is
> `D-[A-Z0-9_]+(-[A-Z0-9_]+){2,}` — **`D-` plus THREE OR MORE `-`-separated segments is a
> DEFERRED-WORK ANCHOR and MUST resolve to a row here; a TWO-segment `D-*` name (`D-OPT`) is an
> informal feature label the guard ignores.** So hyphenating a COMPOUND FEATURE WORD silently changes
> the identifier's CLASS: `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYS-INLINE` tripped the guard and had to be renamed
> `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE` to match its sibling `D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE`. The failure surfaces as
> “missing row”, which misdirects you into WRITING a duplicate row instead of FIXING the name.
> **Spell a compound feature word as ONE segment (`ALWAYSINLINE`, `NOINLINE`); reserve hyphens for
> genuine name components; when in doubt, match the sibling anchor already in this file.** Full
> write-up: [[D-PLANS-ANCHOR-NAME-SEGMENT-COUNT-GATE]].
>

> **★★ MEASUREMENT CAVEAT — READ BEFORE QUOTING ANY “this will clear N errors” NUMBER IN THIS FILE (2026-07-28, macOS-arm64 predefine-probe cycle).** DSS **abandons a TU at its first hard parse failure**, so a corpus error count is a count of the errors REACHED, never of the defects PRESENT. Clearing an early blocker therefore EXPOSES later ones that were never reached, and a drop in the total is NOT a count of defects fixed. Worked example from this cycle: the 189-TU sqlite build went **213 → 80** total errors when architecture + toolchain predefines were both supplied — that is **NOT 133 defects fixed**; the residual 80 is a NEWLY-EXPOSED population whose composition was unknown until separately measured. It is equally possible for a real fix to make the total go UP (this cycle measured exactly that: toolchain-identity macros ALONE took 213 → 216). Every forward estimate of the form “closing X clears N errors” in any row below MUST be read with this caveat, and every new one MUST carry it. See [[D-MEASURE-FIRST-FAILURE-MASKS-RESIDUAL]] for the citable class row.

## Anchor Index

**Row shape: EXACTLY four cells — `Anchor`, `Trigger`, `Closing work`, `Cross-refs`.**
A row with fewer cells shifts every following cell one column LEFT; a row with more
has the surplus SILENTLY DROPPED by the renderer. Neither is visible when reading the
raw text, so the count is load-bearing — see `D-PLANS-REGISTRY-MALFORMED-ROW-CELLS`.

Two authoring rules follow from that, both verified against the GitHub renderer:
- **A raw `|` splits a cell EVEN INSIDE BACKTICKS.** To quote an expression, regex or
  alternation containing one, write `\|` — the backslash-escaped form is the *only*
  one that survives inside a code span (an HTML entity does **not**).
- **` ═══ ` inside a cell marks a seam where two cells were joined** when a row
  authored to a wider schema was converged onto these four columns. It is a joint in
  the prose, not a column boundary.

Windows arm = `_beginthreadex` + `STACK_SIZE_PARAM_IS_A_RESERVATION` + `WaitForSingleObject`/`CloseHandle`; POSIX arm = `pthread_attr_setstacksize`/`pthread_create`/`pthread_join` (CI-verified — no `find_package(Threads)`, raw symbols resolve as `std::thread`'s do). AGNOSTIC: pure host/OS utility, names no language/CPU/format; the `_WIN32`/POSIX `#ifdef` is host-portability. Self-test `tests/core/substrate/test_large_stack_call.cpp` (RunsTheCallable; RethrowsEscapedException value-preserving; ProvidesStackForDeepRecursion = ~1000 frames × `volatile char[8192]` ≈ 8 MB that the default stack can't hold). **KEY EMPIRICAL CORRECTION of the localization below:** wrapping JUST `analyze` was INSUFFICIENT — stage markers in the full c-subset→PE-exec pipeline showed the analyze-wrap lifted the DOWNSTREAM ceiling well past 25 (n=100..180 compile + run clean), but at the raised cap (256) a NEW overflow appeared UPSTREAM: the **CU build (parse / preprocess / type-name oracle)** in `Program::compileFiles`/`compileUnits` (`UnitBuilder::addFile`→`finish`) recurses building the expression tree and overflows the host main stack at ~n=185 (Debug-MSVC) — the low cap (16) had MASKED it (the guard fired at 16, no deep tree was ever built). The Windows x64 ABI REQUIRES a function allocating >1 page to probe each page (`__chkstk`, or an inline `sub rsp,0x1000`/`test [rsp],eax` loop) so the guard page walks down one page at a time and the kernel commits each. Empirically verified: a 400B + a 4400B frame exit 42, a 36000B frame segfaults. Linux x86_64 + AArch64-ELF do NOT need it (kernel stack-growth guard-gap absorbs the multi-page jump — which is why `large_frame_arm64` exits 42 on x86_64-linux + qemu-aarch64). This is WHY the `x86_64:pe64` target was excluded from `examples/c-subset/large_frame_arm64/expected.json` (see its `$comment`). Priority: **normal** (a real silent-crash class on >1-page Windows frames — large local buffers; converting it to FAIL-LOUD is a cheap interim). | Implement Windows large-frame stack probing in the prologue SP-adjust (`lir_callconv.cpp` emitPrologue/emitSpAdjust), gated AGNOSTICALLY on a CC/format-declared stack-probe-threshold field (mirroring `redZoneBytes`/`shadowSpaceBytes`, NOT `if(arch=="x86_64")`): when the frame exceeds the page size, emit the page-walk probe (or a `call __chkstk`) before/in place of the single `sub rsp,N`; add a runtime corpus witness (re-add the `x86_64:pe64` target to `large_frame_arm64`) + a structural pin. The c167/c165 witnesses use single-jump-table + independent (non-calling) 2-function objects, so no baked intra-call is exercised. | `D-TEST-EXAMPLES-RUNNER-PARALLEL-CONTENTION-FLAKE` | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-07-24 (TF-C58 gate — trigger FIRED: it red-ed 3 of 4 consecutive full Win ctest runs, a different example each time). ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is NOT the spawn-timeout fragility this row hypothesized.** The real mechanism is a `ScratchDir` PATH COLLISION (`tests/test_support/scratch_dir.hpp`, shared by every test that needs a scratch dir). The ctor built `<base>/<pid>-<counter>` and called `create_directories`, checking only `ec` and IGNORING the return value — and `create_directories` reports SUCCESS when the directory ALREADY EXISTS. The dtor's `remove_all` swallowed its `ec`, so directories leak whenever a spawned example binary still holds a handle or a run is killed (**55** were sitting in `test-scratch/examples/` when this was found). A process drawing a recycled PID (Windows reuses them freely) plus the same counter value therefore SILENTLY SHARED a stale directory, and the runner's next `copy_file` — which does not pass `overwrite_existing` — threw `filesystem error: cannot copy file: File exists [.../main.c]`. That explains every observed symptom the timeout theory could not: it hits a DIFFERENT example each run, it reproduces in SERIAL runs too (`-j1`, via PID reuse against leaked dirs, not concurrency), it passes on isolated re-run, and it worsens the longer a working tree goes without cleaning `test-scratch/`. **FIX (one chokepoint — both runners and every other ScratchDir consumer inherit it):** the ctor now LOOPS on `create_directory` (singular) and accepts only a slot whose creation it actually won, which is atomic in the OS and therefore race-free across concurrent `ctest -j` processes as well as stale-dir-safe; a bounded attempt cap fails loud naming the accumulation; and the dtor now WARNS on stderr instead of silently swallowing a failed `remove_all`, so leakage is visible while still small. WITNESS: `test_scratch_dir.cpp::StaleDirectoryOnTheNextSlotIsNotReused` plants a populated directory on the exact slot the ctor will draw next (predicted from a probe ScratchDir's own filename, so it pins real ctor behaviour) — **red-on-disable DEMONSTRATED: restoring the return-value-ignoring `create_directories` fails BOTH expectations, while the pre-existing `MultipleScratchDirsGetDistinctPaths` stays GREEN** (it advances the counter either way — an inert pin that was green through the entire lifetime of the bug, the §A.5 trap). | `D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64-NONLEAF-LINK-REGISTER` | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-06-08** — non-leaf ARM64 functions now spill + reload the link register x30. **This is the ACTUAL root cause of the arm64-FFI SIGSEGV (CI exit 139)** that `D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64-FFI-ISEL`'s "→ exit 42" over-claimed away (the prior cycle's self-audit had flagged exactly this runtime risk). A calling convention that carries the return address in a LINK REGISTER (AAPCS64 x30) rather than pushing it on the stack (x86_64 `call`; callPushBytes=8) makes x30 live across the whole body of a non-leaf function — every `bl`/`call` clobbers it. The frame logic spilled the `calleeSaved` set (x19–x29) but NOT x30 (deliberately the `linkRegister`, NOT in `calleeSaved`, so it stays un-allocatable), so `main`'s epilogue `ret` returned to the clobbered LR (the address after the last call) → an infinite self-loop whose repeated epilogue `add sp` walked SP off the stack into a guard page → SIGSEGV. **The FFI dispatch was always correct** — `abs(7-49)` returned 42 in x0; the PLT stub (ADRP x16/LDR x17/BR x17) + the GLOB_DAT relocation both worked. **Fix** (`src/lir/lir_callconv.cpp::materializeOneFunc`, agnostic + config-driven): when `hasCalls && cc.linkRegister.has_value()`, fold the link register into `savedRegs` so the existing prologue/epilogue machinery spills it at entry + reloads it before `ret`. ZERO `if(arch/format==…)` — x86_64 (no `linkRegister`) takes the no-op path; the schema's long-declared `linkRegister` field (whose `target_schema.hpp` comment PROMISED "ML7 lowering checks linkRegister.has_value()") is finally consumed. **Pins**: `LirCallconv.NonLeafAarch64FunctionSpillsLinkRegister` (non-leaf SAVES x30 + leaf does NOT; RED-on-disable: revert the fold → x30 absent → fail) + `LirCallconv.NonLeafX8664FunctionHasNoLinkRegisterToSpill` (agnosticism control: x86_64 cc has no linkRegister → no-op path) + the `extern_call_elf` arm64 runtime corpus (now genuinely exit 42 under qemu + native-arm64; was SIGSEGV → CI red — so red-on-disable by construction). **+ HOST-INDEPENDENT BYTE-PIN (2026-06-08, same-day hardening)**: `LirCallconv.NonLeafAarch64FramePrologueEpilogueByteExact` drives the real production tail (legalizeTwoAddress → materializeCallingConvention → assemble) and byte-pins the ASSEMBLED non-leaf prologue+epilogue EXACT — incl. `stur x30,[sp,#16]` (f80103fe) at prologue offset 12 + `ldur x30,[sp,#16]` (f84103fe) reloaded before `ret` — against hand-verified ARM-ARM literals, plus a leaf-control (g spills x28/x29 but no `stur x30`). RED-on-disable DEMONSTRATED (disable the fold → frame 0x20→0x10 → both byte windows diverge). Closes the gap where the COMPOSED frame's byte-correctness was witnessed ONLY by the native-arm64 runtime leg (the per-instruction arm64 byte-pins prove instructions in isolation, never the composed frame). The THREE layers — structural (savedRegs, every leg) + this byte-pin (assembled bytes, every leg incl. Windows MSVC) + runtime corpus (exit 42, native-arm64 leg) — are complementary; none replaces another. 207/207 (no frame-size regression — x86_64 has no linkRegister so its frames are byte-identical; no arm64 non-leaf frame-size pin existed pre-fix). | (closed) | plan 14 (D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64 family); `D-LK10-ENTRY-ARM64-FFI-ISEL` (the over-claim this corrected); `D-LK10-ENTRY-ML7-FRAME-BIAS-UNIFY` (the frame substrate it extends); `target_schema.hpp` linkRegister field |

| `D-CPP-ERROR-WARNING` | **✅ CLOSED 2026-07-27 (Cycle TF-C70) — C23 `#error` (6.10.5) + `#warning` (6.10.6), config-driven and REACHABILITY-correct.** Closes gap (1) of [[D-CSUBSET-APPLE-SDK-HEADER-SURFACE]]. Before: both words fell through to `P_PreprocessorUnsupported` ("out of FC13 cycle-1 scope") — **50 hits on the macOS sqlite leg, measured as 49 `#error` + 1 `#warning`** (an earlier note said "50 `#error`"; corrected). ★ **THE CRUX IS REACHABILITY, NOT RECOGNITION.** C 6.10.5 makes an `#error` in a NOT-TAKEN `#if` group silent; Apple's SDK headers use `#error` precisely as the unsupported-configuration guard inside branches skipped on a supported target. An implementation firing on every lexed `#error` would turn all 49 into hard user errors and break EVERY macOS compile — strictly worse than the P0015 it replaced. **MECHANISM (agnostic; no engine identity branch):** two OPTIONAL `PreprocessConfig` words `errorDirective`/`warningDirective` (`readOptWord`, the `pragmaDirective`/`embedDirective`/`lineDirective` pattern — there is no `directives` array to extend), valued in `c-subset.lang.json`; two `else if` arms placed INSIDE `handleDirective`'s dispatch chain **below** the `if (!stackActive()) return end;` gate, which makes dead-branch silence structural rather than checked. The arms must NEVER move into the unconditional `#if`-family block above the gate (that block runs in dead regions on purpose, to keep `condStack_` balanced) — stated as an anti-instruction in the code. Two DISTINCT codes `P_PreprocessorErrorDirective`=0x001E / `P_PreprocessorWarningDirective`=0x001F, because `DiagnosticPolicy::suppress` keys on the CODE — one shared code would make `--suppress` of `#warning` noise also silence every `#error`. `emitPP` gained a defaulted trailing severity param (48 pre-existing call sites byte-unchanged: 51 `emitPP(` lines = 1 definition + 50 calls, minus the 2 new arms); `#warning` = Warning, and `hasErrors()`/`pp.fatal` were verified to let the build proceed through compile→link→run. Operand is a RAW source slice, never macro-expanded (gcc/clang parity); a bare `#error` with no operand is legal (`pp-tokens_opt`) and still fires. `P_PreprocessorErrorDirective` is the FIRST `P_*` member of `unsuppressable_codes` (all 127 prior entries are D_/F_/H_/I_/K_/L_/R_/A_/S_ (the table is 128 with this one)) — a user-authored abort must not be suppressible into a silently-built invalid configuration; a new tier line documents the family break. **★ HONEST NET EFFECT — do not misread the next corpus run:** all 49 `#error` sites are in LIVE branches (DSS predefines no `__GNUC__`/`__clang__`/`__x86_64__`/`__arm64__` — grep-verified 0), so this cycle **re-codes 49 P0015 → 49 P001E at the same 49 sites** rather than clearing them: 153 → ~152. That is the point — the old message was an actively misleading lie ("DSS lacks this directive") sent users hunting a missing feature instead of a genuinely-rejected configuration. **The only site this cycle actually CLEARS is the `#warning` at `sys/cdefs.h:81`** (live under `#if !defined(__GNUC__)`), and since nearly every Apple header includes `sys/cdefs.h`, dropping it from Error to Warning is the load-bearing half. The real closer for the 49 is the compiler/arch identity predefines — §B-decided 2026-07-27 to be its own cycle, tracked under [[D-CSUBSET-DARWIN-PLATFORM-MACROS]] (note it needs a per-**ARCH** gate, which `availableObjectFormats` cannot express today — it keys on object FORMAT). **TESTS: 16 `TfC70*` pins, two-directional by construction** — an implementation that fires on every lexed `#error` is caught by the four silence pins (`#if 0`, `#ifdef` undefined, not-taken `#else`, nested dead-outer/live-inner); one that never fires is caught by the positive twins; a hardcoded `"error"` literal is caught by the REBIND pins (`errorDirective`→`"errr"`, then `#error`→P0015 and `#errr`→P001E — a strip-only test would NOT catch it, which is why the design audit rejected the original plan's version as config-theatre). ★ Two spec errors were caught by the test author and are recorded so they are not re-introduced: (i) the nesting test does NOT uniquely prove `sbStackActive` walks every frame — `sbHandleIf` pushes `thisBranchActive = enclosing && cond`, making the innermost check and the full walk observationally equivalent BY CONSTRUCTION, so no test can separate them; (ii) the originally-specified pre-scan test source was INERT (a dead-branch prose `#define` is never harvested, because the pre-scan's define arm is already `sbStackActive`-gated) and was replaced with three empirically-reproduced sub-cases. ★★ (iii) **A MULTI-FORM COVERAGE MISS, caught only by the corpus author and fixed in-cycle — the most instructive failure of the three.** `directiveOperandText` DROPPED THE CLOSING STRING DELIMITER whenever the operand ENDED in a literal: `#warning "Unsupported compiler detected"` reported `#warning: "Unsupported compiler detected` — no closing quote — violating C23 6.10.5p1/6.10.6's verbatim-pp-tokens requirement **on `sys/cdefs.h:81`, the exact shape that motivated the entire feature**. ROOT CAUSE: the tokenizer splits a literal into a `StringStart` token holding ONLY the opening quote plus a COALESCED BODY token covering the bytes BETWEEN the quotes, so the closing quote belongs to NO token's span and a first..last `SourceSpan::join` stops one byte short. The quote-INCLUDE path already solved this identically (`if (dirEnd < spliced.size() && spliced[dirEnd] == dquote) ++dirEnd;`) — the new helper simply did not copy it. FIX: re-consume the trailing byte, GUARDED on it actually being `"` or `'` so a stray unpaired quote (`#error abc"`, already covered by its StringStart's own span) can never gain a phantom character. ★ WHY ALL 13 PINS MISSED IT: every one used BARE PROSE, and `"abc" tail` also passes because the join ends on `tail` — so the suite was green over a SUBSET of the operand FORMS while the single most important form was broken. A gap in the list is a shipped false bug report.** ⭐⭐ **★★★★ WHAT THE CENSUS MEASURED — ~3100 SDK HEADERS + 52 SQLITE HEADERS — AND THE LIST WAS INCOMPLETE IN *TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS*, EACH OF WHICH WOULD HAVE SHIPPED EXACTLY THE FALSE COMPILER BUG THE REQUIREMENT EXISTED TO PREVENT.** **(GAP 1) THE GUARD IS NOT ALWAYS THE FIRST CONDITIONAL.** ✔MEASURED: **11 headers open with an UMBRELLA CHECK before the guard** (`netinet6/in6.h` is the named exemplar). **Any detector that examines "the first conditional" — the obvious implementation of a shape list — misses all 11.** **(GAP 2) `#ifndef X` / `#define X` IS *ALSO* THE IDIOM FOR VALUE DEFAULTS.** ✔MEASURED in `btreeInt.h`: the canonical guard shape and the canonical default-value shape are **LEXICALLY IDENTICAL**. ★★ **So naive shape-matching does not merely MISS guards — it INVENTS them, classifying a value default as an include guard. A shape list is wrong in BOTH directions at once, and the second direction is invisible until it misfires.** ⚠ **AND TWO ITEMS THE LIST NAMED TURNED OUT TO BE LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN THEORETICAL:** compound MIXED-polarity guards are not a hypothetical — they are present **IN THE SQLITE CORPUS ITSELF** (`ext/misc/windirent.h` uses `#if defined(_WIN32) && !defined(N)`; `ext/session/sqlite3session.h` mixes polarity the other way); and `#pragma once` is the **SOLE** include-once mechanism for **21 SDK headers**, so it could not be deferred as an edge case. ⭐⭐⭐ **★★★★★ THE RESOLUTION — AND IT *DISSOLVES* THE REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN SATISFYING IT.** ✔TREE-VERIFIED, the shipped rule is: **A HEADER CARRIES A MACRO INCLUDE GUARD IFF, FOR SOME NAME `N`, THE HEADER `#define`s `N` INSIDE A CONDITIONAL REGION WHOSE *CONTROLLING LINE MENTIONS* `N`.** ★★ **"Mentions" is PURELY LEXICAL — is the Word `N` among the controlling line's tokens. NO `!` parsing. NO `defined` parsing. NO shape vocabulary AT ALL.** ⭐ **IT COVERS EVERY MEASURED SPELLING WITH ONE RULE** — canonical (2942 SDK, 35 sqlite) · `#if !defined(N)` (10 SDK, 1 sqlite) · unparenthesised `#if !defined N` (10+) · triple-negative compounds (`pcap/bpf.h`) · both mixed-polarity sqlite forms · `#define` up to 5 lines later (15 measured) · guard-not-first (11 measured) — **AND IT COVERS SPELLINGS NOBODY HAS MEASURED YET, because the rule tracks what a guard *IS* rather than how anyone has happened to write one.** ★ **It also dissolves GAP 2 for free: a value default `#define`s a name its controlling line mentions but does so to SUPPLY a value, and the rule's scope — the header's own include-once behaviour — is decided by whether re-entry empties the body, which the detector then hands to the real conditional logic.** ⛔⛔ **★★★★★ THE SAFETY CLAUSE — RECORD IT, CITE IT, AND DO NOT LET A FUTURE CYCLE QUIETLY INVALIDATE IT: OVER-RECOGNITION IS SAFE *ONLY BECAUSE RE-ENTRY IS PERMITTED, NOT SKIPPED*.** If the detector wrongly calls something a guard, the body is spliced again and the REAL conditional logic decides, with the depth cap as backstop — **cost: nothing.** ★★ **HAD THE DESIGN *SKIPPED* THE INCLUDE INSTEAD, over-recognition would SILENTLY DROP CONTENT A REAL CPP WOULD HAVE INCLUDED — a silent miscompile, and the one outcome worth engineering against. THE GENEROUS RULE AND THE PERMIT-DON'T-SKIP DECISION ARE A SINGLE DESIGN; NEITHER IS SOUND ALONE.** ⛔ **ANY future change from PERMIT to SKIP silently converts this detector from safely-generous to a silent-miscompile channel, and nothing in the code will complain. THAT IS THE THING TO GUARD.** | ★★★ **NO CLOSING WORK — SHIPPED. WHAT THIS ROW OWES THE FUTURE IS THE LESSON, STATED GENERALLY BECAUSE IT IS NOT ABOUT INCLUDE GUARDS.** ⭐⭐ **★★★★ WHEN A REQUIREMENT IS "ENUMERATE EVERY SHAPE OF X", THE BETTER ANSWER IS USUALLY *A FORMULATION FOR WHICH SHAPE IS IRRELEVANT*.** ★★ **A shape list has three properties that make it a bad acceptance criterion, all three MEASURED here rather than argued: (i) it is INCOMPLETE and you cannot know by how much — the census found 2 gaps in a list written by someone who had thought carefully about it; (ii) it is wrong in BOTH DIRECTIONS — it misses real instances AND invents false ones, and the false-positive direction is the one nobody tests for; (iii) it ROTS — every new spelling in the wild silently degrades it, with no signal, because a shape list cannot report its own coverage.** ★ **A definitional rule has none of the three. Before accepting an enumeration as a spec, ask what the thing IS, and whether that can be tested directly.** ⚠ **THE COUNTER-DISCIPLINE, so this lesson is not over-applied: a definitional rule is only better if it is CHECKABLE and if its FAILURE MODE IS BENIGN. Here both hold — the rule is a lexical test, and over-recognition is free BECAUSE re-entry is permitted. ★★ A definitional rule whose over-recognition SILENTLY DROPPED code would be far worse than a shape list. THE FAILURE-MODE ANALYSIS IS NOT OPTIONAL; IT IS WHAT LICENSES THE GENEROSITY.** ⭐ **STANDING OBLIGATION FOR ANY CYCLE TOUCHING THIS AREA: if you change re-entry from PERMITTED to SKIPPED, or add a code path where a detected "guard" causes the include to be dropped rather than re-spliced, THE SAFETY ARGUMENT IS VOID and the detector must be re-derived, not merely re-tested.** ⚠ **A test that only asserts "these guard shapes are recognised" would stay GREEN through exactly that change — [[D-TEST-REDONDISABLE-DECAY]]'s shape, one tier up.** | created 2026-07-29 (TF-C87 anchor pass, at close, working tree from HEAD `5093341`). **PARENT:** [[D-PP-INCLUDE-REENTRY-GUARD-AWARE]] (this is the refutation of that row's central acceptance criterion). **SIBLING DESIGN RECORDS — rows that exist because the REJECTED option is the instructive one:** [[D-OPT-NOOPTIMIZE-NEUTERS-POLICY]] · [[D-CSUBSET-TOOLCHAIN-IDENTITY-PREDEFINES]] (the `{{version}}` placeholder that was pre-registered and then rejected). **METHOD SIBLINGS:** [[D-PLANS-ANCHOR-EXPECTATION-BECOMES-SPEC]] (an expectation hardening into a spec — THIS row is the healthy outcome, where the expectation was MEASURED and then discarded) · [[D-GATE-CORPUS-MEASURE-INSTRUMENT-INVALID]] (measure before believing). **AGNOSTICISM NOTE, ✔TREE-VERIFIED and worth keeping because it is the kind of claim that rots:** every directive word comes from `PreprocessConfig` (`ifDirective` / `ifndefDirective` / `elif*` / `endifDirective` / `defineDirective` / `pragmaDirective`), and `#pragma once` is recognised through the `pragmaEffects` REGISTRY's `includeOnce` verb, **never through the literal word `once`**. So the fail-loud was a SYMPTOM of compiling the wrong platform branch, not a missing constant, and "add `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` for macho" would have been a WORKAROUND that cemented the wrong arm. ★★ THE REAL SEVERITY IS SILENT, NOT LOUD: here the wrong branch happened to reference an unavailable constant and failed loudly — lucky. Every OTHER `#ifdef __APPLE__` across a 189-TU corpus (os_unix.c's `F_FULLFSYNC`/`F_PREALLOCATE` paths, mmap/fcntl selection, and any third-party header) silently took the NON-Apple arm and would have compiled to valid-but-wrong-for-the-platform code. That cascade is the CORRECT direction — it is what a real Darwin compile does — and is measured by re-running the corpus. ═══ ★ GENERAL RULE: a target's **platform-announcement macros are part of its ABI contract**, not a nicety — omitting them does not disable platform code, it silently selects the WRONG platform code. A corpus error count is therefore a count of the errors **REACHED**, never of the defects **PRESENT**. Clearing an early blocker does not only remove its errors — it **EXPOSES** later defects in the same TU that the compiler never got far enough to report. ⭐⭐ **THE TWO WAYS THIS MISLEADS, both MEASURED (RELAYED) this cycle on the 189-TU sqlite build:** **(1) a drop is not a fix-count.** Architecture + toolchain predefines took the total **213 → 80**. When such a token is the SUBJECT of a parse error, that span reaches the renderer verbatim. On the exact repro **7 diagnostics carried offsets 71 through 117 against a 50-byte source**, so the walk read up to **67 bytes past the end of the buffer** into live adjacent heap (dumped bytes `55 31`, `2d 14` — not ASCII, i.e. it was reading other allocations). ★★ **THE NON-DETERMINISM IS EXPLAINED — THE MECHANISM IS THE POINT, recorded so nobody re-opens a "flaky abort" hunt:** the abort fires **if and only if a `'\n'` (0x0A) happens to sit in the recycled-heap window past the buffer**. If one does, the walk stops with `lineStart > size()` and `substr` throws; if none does, the walk continues back INTO the buffer and renders fine. That window is freed-and-reused heap, so its contents differ per run — hence roughly 3 in 20, **higher under load** (more allocator churn) and **never under lldb**, which disables ASLR and hands out fresh zeroed pages. ★ **It was NOT unordered_map iteration order** — the hypothesis in the user report — nor an ordering effect of any kind. ★★ **THE ASYMMETRY THAT ALLOWED IT, AND THE GENERALISABLE POINT: ONE MEMBER OF A CLAMPING FAMILY NEVER GOT THE TREATMENT EVERY SIBLING GOT.** ✔TREE `SourceBuffer::lineCol` already clamps with `std::min(byteOffset, size())` (source_buffer.cpp:115) and `extractLine` CALLS it one line above the unclamped walk; `SourceBuffer::slice` clamps both ends (:105-111); `SourceReader::slice` clamps both ends (source_reader.cpp:19-25). | `D-CSUBSET-BUILTIN-SHADOWED-BY-PROTOTYPE-REVERTS-TO-EXTERN` | 🔴 **OPEN — normal — created 2026-07-31 (TF-C106), found by the IMPLEMENTING agent while probing, not by a failing gate.** ★ **MEASURED: a builtin declared in `builtinFunctions[]` is SHADOW-ABLE, so a translation unit that merely PROTOTYPES the same name turns every call back into an ORDINARY EXTERN REFERENCE.** The agent reproduced it deliberately: prototyping `_byteswap_ushort` in the TU produced **3× `K_SymbolUndefined`** where the builtin lowering had been emitting `bswap` instructions. ⓘ **Shadowing is the CORRECT C semantics** (a user declaration must win over a compiler builtin — that is why the mechanism exists), so this row is NOT a bug report against the shadowing rule. **THE HAZARD IS THE FAILURE MODE:** the call silently stops being a lowered instruction and becomes a link/load-time dependency on a symbol that, for this family, **DOES NOT EXIST** — `msvcrt.dll` exports no `_byteswap_*` (measured by `objdump -p`, with memcpy/_msize/puts as positive controls), and DSS eager-imports declared symbols, so the pe64 outcome is `STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND (0xC0000139)` AT LOAD rather than a compile error. ⚠ **SQLITE IS SAFE TODAY, and only by a hair:** it reaches these names through `#pragma intrinsic(...)`, which NAMES without DECLARING (`realizationRequestOnly`) — so nothing prototypes them. ★★ **THE LIVE TRAP: a REAL MSVC `<intrin.h>` DOES prototype the whole family, and `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/intrin.json` is deliberately a near-empty stub.** Anyone who "completes" that descriptor by adding the honest prototypes — an obviously reasonable-looking improvement — silently converts every byteswap in the corpus from an instruction into an unresolvable import, and the pe64 leg dies at LOAD with no compile diagnostic. That is precisely the shape [[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]] exists to warn about, arriving from the opposite direction. | (1) Put a LOUD warning in `intrin.json`'s `$comment` stating that the `_byteswap_*` / `__builtin_bswap*` family must NEVER be given prototypes there, and WHY (prototype ⇒ shadow ⇒ extern ⇒ eager import ⇒ 0xC0000139 at load, because no CRT exports them). (2) Decide the general policy and make it enforceable: either (a) DIAGNOSE the collision — when a user/descriptor declaration shadows a builtin whose lowering has NO importable symbol behind it, emit a real warning naming both, so the silent conversion becomes visible; or (b) let a descriptor mark such names UNSHADOWABLE. ★ (a) is preferred: it keeps C's shadowing semantics intact and only makes the CONSEQUENCE visible, which is the fail-loud posture this project takes elsewhere. (3) Red-on-disable is cheap and exact: a TU that prototypes `_byteswap_ushort` and calls it must produce the chosen diagnostic; today it produces `K_SymbolUndefined` at best and a LOAD failure at worst. Trigger: FIRED (reproduced on demand); no corpus consumer today. Priority: normal — nothing is broken now, but the trap is baited and the bait looks like an improvement. | [[D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP]] (the family that made it reachable) · [[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]] (why an undeclared-but-imported symbol is fatal at LOAD, not link) · `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/intrin.json` (the stub that must stay a stub for this family) |

A compiler explains itself on stderr; that explanation went nowhere, so a one-shot failure was undiagnosable at the moment it mattered. ★ **THE IRONY IS THE POINT AND IS WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A NICETY:** this file exists BECAUSE a probe once conflated "no compiler installed" with "a step broke", and its whole design is about keeping statuses apart — `ToolAbsent` vs `ToolQueryFailed` vs `CompileFailed` vs `ExecutableMissing` vs `RunFailed` vs `OutputUnreadable` vs `EmptyOutput`. It distinguishes WHICH step broke meticulously and then drops WHY for the one step that can say. **FIX, IN TWO PARTS — AND THE SECOND WAS ONLY FOUND BY EXERCISING THE FIRST:** (1) a `captureCmd()` sibling to the existing `redirectCmd()` — it appends `> log 2>&1` to an ALREADY-ASSEMBLED command line instead of quoting a path (quoting the vcvars `&&` chain again would corrupt it), keeping cmd.exe's outer-quote rule for the same reason `redirectCmd` keeps it — plus `tailOf()`, which folds the last 30 lines into the detail and keeps **unreadable / empty / present** as three distinct answers rather than collapsing them to `""`. `build.empty()` stays FIRST in the `\|\|` so `captureCmd` is never handed an empty command. ★★ (2) **THE MSVC BATCH WAS SILENCING `cl` ITSELF.** The generated `build_probe.bat` ended its compile line with `>nul 2>&1`, so the capture collected an EMPTY log and reported "the build command produced NO output at all" — ✔which is precisely what it said the first time the arm was exercised. The capture was correct and was pointed at a stream already emptied one level down. `cl`'s silencer is removed; `call vcvars` keeps its own, because on success it prints a pure-noise banner and its failure is already covered upstream by `locateMsvcToolchain`. ⓘ **THAT ORDERING IS THE LESSON:** part (1) alone would have shipped looking finished, and its output — the honest string "NO output at all" — would have been read as "the compiler said nothing", which is false. Only running the failure arm distinguished them. ✔**DEMONSTRATED END-TO-END:** with a deliberate syntax error injected into the emitted `probe.c`, the message now carries `probe.c(3): error C2018: character 'U+40' is not permitted here` and eight more lines, file and line included; mutation reverted byte-identical (sha256) and both ABI witnesses re-run green. ⚠ **THE RISK IS SHELL QUOTING AND IT IS LOUD, NOT SILENT:** get it wrong and the build fails on every host and every run — checked on Windows (cmd.exe) and under WSL (POSIX sh) both. That is the opposite of the failure mode this file warns about, where a wrong redirection SILENTLY became "no compiler installed". ★ **THE ONE-SHOT FAILURE THAT EXPOSED THIS IS A SEPARATE, STILL-OPEN QUESTION — see [[D-TEST-NATIVE-PROBE-COMPILE-FAILS-UNDER-CONCURRENT-LOAD]].** This row closes the DIAGNOSTIC gap only; it does not explain the failure, and must not be read as having done so. | Cross-refs: `tests/core/native_c_probe.hpp` (`captureCmd`, `tailOf`, and the capture at the CompileFailed arm) · `tests/core/test_packed_abi_conformance.cpp` (the witness that hit it) · [[D-TEST-FIXED-SCRATCH-PATH-POPULATION]] (ruled OUT as the cause here: `ScratchDir` claims its directory atomically with `create_directory`, so a collision is excluded by construction) |

## Allowlist (code-internal pins, NOT deferred work)

Anchor-shaped strings in `src/` that are **not** deferred-work markers and
should be **ignored** by the CI guard. Add a row when an in-code constant
or diagnostic-message identifier matches the `D-*` regex but isn't a
deferred-work anchor.

| Pattern | Reason |
|---|---|
| `D-MERGE-GLOBAL-INITFUNC` | Cycle 25 Stage B code-internal INVARIANT pin (`src/mir/merge/mir_merge.cpp`), NOT deferred work. Cited in the fail-loud abort that fires if a merged global's `initFunc` MirFuncId was not cloned into the merged module (`plan.funcMerged` miss). The invariant always holds for valid input — a global's module-init function is a defined function in the same CU, which the merge always clones (an init function is never a cross-CU weak loser). The abort is defense-in-depth: a breach means the planning pass dropped a function a global still references (a structural contradiction), so failing loud beats emitting a global whose initializer points at a stale/absent func. No closing work — it is a permanent guard, like the other `mergeFatal` invariant aborts. |

NO base choice is correct in the fixed-reservation model. Closing work: the NON-LEAF VLA frame model — a §B-worthy design (outgoing-args placed BELOW where the VLA goes, or a separate outgoing-args pointer; or over-allocate + a two-region frame). | `D-CSUBSET-VLA-FOR-INIT-SCOPE` | ✅ **LANDED 2026-07-14 (VLA C5) — a for-INIT VLA (`for (int a[n]; …; )`) now gets FULL for-scope block teardown.** (This anchor was briefly a fail-loud DEFERRAL earlier in this SAME cycle; the code-audit correctly flagged that gate as a REGRESSION — a top-level for-init VLA compiled + RAN pre-C5, function-scoped + epilogue-freed — and it contradicted the user OPTION-C full-general-teardown directive, so it was replaced with real teardown before the cycle closed. The prior "leaks per-iteration" rationale was factually wrong for a top-level for-init.) MECHANISM: a for-init VLA is declared ONCE at loop entry and PERSISTS across all iterations; C5 frees it ONLY on the loop-EXIT edges, NEVER on the back-edge (freeing it there = a use-after-free of `a[]` in iteration 2+). `emitStackSaveForVla` accepts a `ForStmt` scope node (single-declarator for-init: `hir.parent(declNode) == ForStmt`); the For driver captures the VLA watermark BEFORE the init (`f.vlaBase`), so the for-init frame sits at exactly `vlaBase` and the BODY block's per-iteration teardown (whose watermark is DEEPER, captured after the init) can never reach it (the depth bookkeeping keeps them distinct). The For driver emits ONE StackRestore at the loop EXIT block (the merge of the cond-false edge + every `break` — a break already restored the body VLAs to the post-init watermark, so both predecessors arrive with SP at the post-init level); `continue` frees only body VLAs (post-init watermark), keeping the for-init live; a `goto` OUT of the loop restores the for-init via the ancestry walk (`vlaFrameEnclosesLabel` treats a ForStmt scope as whole-for). Pins: `ForInitVlaEmitsForScopeTeardownAtLoopExitOnly` (for-init-only → 1 save + 1 restore, NONE on the back-edge) + `ForInitAndBodyVlaTornDownAtDistinctPoints` (for-init + body VLA → 2 restores in DIFFERENT blocks) + the `c99_vla_loop` phase-6 runtime witness (a for-init VLA in a 400000-iteration outer loop, written at k=0 + read at k>0 — catches BOTH a back-edge-free [use-after-free → wrong total] AND a leak [overflow]). Multi-declarator for-init VLAs remain deferred → `D-CSUBSET-VLA-FOR-INIT-MULTIDECL`. |
| `D-CSUBSET-VLA-FOR-INIT-MULTIDECL` | ⏳ **GATED — normal (opened 2026-07-14, VLA C5; src-cited `hir_to_mir.cpp` `emitStackSaveForVla`).** A VLA in a MULTI-declarator for-init clause (`for (int a[n], b[m]; …)`) is FAILED LOUD at HIR→MIR (H at the VarDecl), NEVER a silent early-free. WHY: cst_to_hir wraps a multi-declarator for-init in a `Block` of VarDecls (whose parent is the ForStmt); that Block is lowered via `lowerForClauseNode` during For phase 0 and drains fully (its own Block-scope teardown fires) BEFORE the loop header/body — so a VLA there would be freed at the END OF THE INIT, before the first iteration (a use-after-free for the whole loop). The single-declarator for-init (`for (int a[n]; …)`, the common form, `hir.parent == ForStmt`) gets full for-scope teardown (D-CSUBSET-VLA-FOR-INIT-SCOPE). Detection: `emitStackSaveForVla` recognizes the wrapper by `hir.kind(scopeNode)==Block && hir.parent(scopeNode)==ForStmt && hir.forInit(that)==scopeNode`. Closing work: give the for-init wrapper Block for-scope (not block-scope) teardown semantics — push its VLAs onto the vlaScopeStack without the Block driver's per-exit restore, and free them at the For driver's loop-exit. Trigger: a real multi-declarator-for-init-VLA need. |

ROOT CAUSE: `boundary="$(files_after … \| head -1)"` returns **141 (SIGPIPE)** whenever `files_after` yields MORE THAN ONE line — `head` closes the pipe — and the driver runs under `set -Eeuo pipefail`, so a non-zero pipeline status is FATAL. ⇒ **the harness survived the fixture's abort and was then killed by its own resume helper.** ★★ **THE SHAPE IS WHY IT SURVIVED SO LONG, and it is the inverse of the usual bug:** it fails on the **NORMAL** case (matches exist → 141) and returns **0** on the **EMPTY** one (no matches). A defect that is correct in its edge case and broken in its common case is invisible to exactly the testing that edge cases attract. ⚠ **MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS RIGHT AND MY FIRST TWO REPROS REFUTED IT** — 3 lines and then 5000 synthetic lines both returned rc=0, because awk finished writing before `head` closed.
